landmarks.name: Pyramids of Meroë
landmarks.writeup: Ancient Nubian pyramids located in the northeastern region, showcasing the Kingdom of Kush's rich history.

landmarks.name: Jebel Barkal
landmarks.writeup: A small mountain considered sacred, surrounded by archaeological sites linked to the ancient Kingdom of Napata.

landmarks.name: Suakin Island
landmarks.writeup: Historic Red Sea port with Ottoman-era ruins reflecting Sudan's maritime trade history.

head_of_state: General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan (Chairman of the Transitional Sovereignty Council)

cultural_events.name: Sufi Festivals
cultural_events.writeup: Religious gatherings featuring traditional music and dance, celebrating Sudan's Sufi Islamic heritage.

cultural_events.name: Khartoum International Book Fair
cultural_events.writeup: Annual event promoting literature and cultural exchange in Sudan.

food_writeup: Sudanese cuisine blends Arab and African influences, featuring dishes like ful medames (stewed fava beans), kisra (fermented bread), and tagine-style stews with meat and vegetables.
brief_history: Sudan has a history dating back to ancient Nubian kingdoms. It was colonized by the British and Egyptians in the 19th century and gained independence in 1956. The country has experienced civil wars, the secession of South Sudan in 2011, and ongoing political transitions.

important_people.name: Omar al-Bashir
important_people.description: Former president who ruled from 1989 to 2019

important_people.name: Sadiq al-Mahdi
important_people.description: Former Prime Minister and opposition leader

current_conflicts: Sudan faces internal conflicts including clashes in Darfur, South Kordofan, and Blue Nile regions, as well as political instability following the 2019 revolution.
